To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the active-site helices of the thiol–disulfide oxidoredoctase DsbA are flexible in terms of sequence and that this flexibility is crucial for the function of DsbA.
the catalytic properties of the active-site cysteines of DsbA can be altered by randomizing the active-site helices α1 and α2.

(i) DsbA variants that are more oxidizing than the wild type are still functional, (ii) DsbA is functional even when the entire active-site helix is randomized, and (iii) the active-site helices of DsbA and DsbB can be interchanged without loss of function, indicating that the two proteins are very similar in their active-site structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of the catalytic activity of DsbA, and we have found that DsbA variants with a redox potential below −210 mVolts are not able to complement DsbA-deficiency.
the design of a new class of proteins, which are active in vivo, but have a much reduced redox potential compared to DsbA.
the design and construction of a large number of active DsbA variants with altered reactivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DsbA can tolerate extensive non-conservative changes in helix α1, as long as the helical secondary structure is preserved.
the redox potential of DsbA is a poor indicator for its in vivo activity.
the tertiary structure of the entire active-site helix of DsbA is essential for its function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the active-site helices of thiol-disulfides oxidoreductases are highly conserved and that a high redox potential is not required for the in vivo activity of DsbA.
the catalytic disulphide of DsbA is very robust against sequence variations and that the redox potential of the catalytic site is not the only determinant of its activity in vivo.

the tertiary structure context strongly influences the secondary structure formation of helix α 1, but the tertiary structure context is not the only determinant for the redox potential and catalytic properties of DsbA.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tertiary structure context strongly influences the secondary structure propensity of randomized sequences, and that the tertiary structure of the randomized protein is more important than the sequence for its activity.
a single active site helix can accommodate a large number of sequence variants that are active in protein folding.
a single helix in the protein can tolerate a large number of replacements, provided that the tertiary structure is not disturbed.
